newsitem.title: INDIA: Profit-taking drags down Delhi shares.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking drags down Delhi shares.

text.p: Delhi share prices drifted lower on Friday as profit-taking by speculators and domestic financial institutions wiped out early gains on the last day of the current settlement period, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index ended 2.01 points lower at 910.46.
"Today's session was mainly of a squaring-off nature as most players were seen settling their positions," said Shree Bhagwan Garg of brokers Means Leasing.
Traders said the drop in share prices was expected.
"The drop in highly active share prices was a technical correction which is a healthy sign for a capital market," said another broker.
Reliance Industries closed 8.25 rupees lower at 355.50.
State Bank of India rose 3.80 rupees to 351.20 on buying by foreign institutional investors.
Hero Honda gained 37 rupees to 607 as it entered a no-delivery period for the next month.
Larsen and Toubro increased five rupees to 255.25.
